# Alchemy

Infrastructure as Effects (Alchemy v2): infra/alchemy.run.ts declares the Worker and its bindings instead of wrangler.jsonc, with PR preview stages deployed from GitHub Actions.

Id `infra/alchemy`. It fills the Infrastructure as code slot: a project makes one Infrastructure as code choice, or none. Template: [`templates/infra/alchemy/`](../../templates/infra/alchemy/).

## What it is for

Declares the Worker and its bindings in TypeScript, in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`, instead of `wrangler.jsonc`, which it removes. `pnpm dev` and `pnpm run deploy` go through Alchemy, and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys a preview stage for each pull request.

## Add it

When you create the project:

```sh
npm create efforge my-app -- --infra=alchemy
```

Add it to an existing project whose `infra` is `none`:

```sh
npx create-efforge add infra/alchemy
```

## Needs

Nothing else.

## Conflicts with

Nothing.

## Service and layer

None: this add-on adds no service of its own.

## Files it writes

`efforge add` writes these files. A file marked *replaces* is one efforge generated before; it is replaced only if you have not edited it, and otherwise `add` changes nothing and shows the diff. A file marked *only if missing* is written only where the project lacks it.

- `infra/alchemy.run.ts`
- `infra/tsconfig.json`
- `infra/README.md`
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- `apps/web/vite.config.ts` (*replaces*)
- `apps/web/regions.ts` (*only if missing*)

It removes `wrangler.jsonc`, because `infra/alchemy.run.ts` declares the Worker instead. If you edited `wrangler.jsonc`, `add` stops and shows the diff.

## Files it edits

`efforge add` makes these edits with AST transforms (changes to the parsed code, not to its text), so it changes only what is listed and leaves the rest of each file alone.

### `AGENTS.md`

- Adds the rules under [Rules it adds to AGENTS.md](#rules-it-adds-to-agentsmd).

### `package.json`

- Adds the dependencies listed below.
- Sets the scripts `dev`, `typecheck`, `deploy`, `destroy`; a script of the same name is replaced.

### `pnpm-workspace.yaml`

- Pins the new dependencies in the `catalog`.

### `apps/web/package.json`

- Sets the script `deploy`; a script of the same name is replaced.

### `.env.example`

- Adds the environment variables listed below.

### `efforge.jsonc`

- Records the add-on in the stack and the hashes of the files it wrote.

## Environment variables

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, for example `your-account-id`: Needed by `pnpm run deploy`, with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; `pnpm exec alchemy provider check-env -c infra/alchemy.run.ts` checks both.

## Package scripts

- `dev` in `package.json`: `alchemy dev infra/alchemy.run.ts`
- `typecheck` in `package.json`: `turbo run typecheck && tsc -p infra`
- `deploy` in `package.json`: `alchemy deploy infra/alchemy.run.ts`
- `destroy` in `package.json`: `alchemy destroy infra/alchemy.run.ts`
- `deploy` in `apps/web/package.json`: `pnpm --workspace-root run deploy`

## Rules it adds to AGENTS.md

### Infrastructure (Alchemy)

- `infra/alchemy.run.ts` declares the Worker and every resource it binds. There is no `wrangler.jsonc`: add a binding as a resource there and pass it in the `env` of `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`, under the name effect-cf reads. `efforge add` inserts resources above `// efforge:resources`; keep that line.
- Settings come from `Config` calls in `alchemy.run.ts`: from `.env` under `pnpm dev`, and from `--env-file` or the environment when deploying. Never write a secret's value into `alchemy.run.ts`, and never commit `.env` or `.env.production`.
- `pnpm dev` runs stage `dev_$USER`; `pnpm run deploy --stage <name>` creates or updates a stage and `pnpm run destroy --stage <name>` removes one. Write `pnpm run deploy`: `pnpm deploy` is pnpm's own command.
- Local state lives in `.alchemy/` (gitignored); CI keeps it in a Cloudflare-hosted store. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys `main` to `prod` and each pull request to `pr-<number>`: a new setting the Worker reads goes in its `env` and in the repository secrets.
- `pnpm typecheck` checks `infra/` too (`tsc -p infra`).

## Limits

- It uses an Alchemy 2.0 beta; the exact version is under Dependencies.
- Local secrets are read from `.env`, not `.dev.vars`.
- On D1, `pnpm db:migrate` still expects a `wrangler.jsonc`.
